CHIEF COMPLAINT
Difficulty swallowing and chest pain with swallowing.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports difficulty swallowing for several weeks, particularly with larger pieces of food. He describes pain with swallowing that occurs most of the time, localized to the chest. Symptoms are worse with bigger food pieces. Patient denies weight loss; reports weight gain over the past month instead. Denies blood in stool or dark tarry stools. Patient attributes stress to recent move from west coast to east coast over the past couple of months, during which he has been eating more fast foods including pizza and burgers. Occasional epigastric pain reported.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies abdominal pain except for occasional epigastric discomfort. Denies nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Denies blood in stool or dark tarry stools.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is relocating from west coast to east coast, which he reports is stressful. Has a dog and considering driving for the move due to concerns about air travel for the pet. Recent increased consumption of fast food (pizza, burgers) due to stress from move.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure 133/70, heart rate normal, no fever, respiratory rate 19, oxygen saturation 100%. Weight gain of approximately 10 pounds over the past month. No ulcers or thrush in mouth. Tonsils midline. No neck adenopathy or thyromegaly. Abdomen nondistended with active bowel sounds. Pain to palpation of epigastric area. Negative Murphy's sign, no peritoneal signs, no rebound. Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally. No rash, lesions, or bruising. Eyes equal and reactive to light.

RESULTS
Barium swallow showed two areas of mild narrowing in the mid and lower portions of the esophagus consistent with esophagitis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Acute esophagitis. Prescribed Protonix 40 mg once daily in the morning. Prescribed Carafate 1 gram four times daily for one month to coat esophageal and gastric lining. Patient advised to change diet, decrease alcohol and caffeine intake, eat slowly, and chew food more thoroughly. Avoid citrus fruits and spicy foods until symptoms improve. Upper endoscopy scheduled for next week. Follow-up visit scheduled for next week.
